edges.description: Acute loss of TUBGCP6 reduced centrosome-driven microtubule nucleation in DLD-1 cells. Application to germline patient alleles is model extrapolation.
Acute endogenous TUBGCP6 degradation caused centriole-duplication failure in DLD-1 cells, and a TUBGCP6 transgene rescued that experimental defect.
Reduced nucleation and monopolar-spindle arrest co-occurred after the same depletion; the experiment did not isolate nucleation as the sole mediator.
Centriole-duplication failure and monopolar-spindle arrest co-occurred after TUBGCP6 depletion, but the paper did not isolate their causal ordering.
The mitotic deficits reduced proliferation in the same cell model.
The cellular model and human cerebral phenotype are consistent with this bridge, but no TUBGCP6 neural-development experiment establishes it.
intermediate_mechanisms: Developmental neural-progenitor loss or dysfunction is hypothesized but untested in TUBGCP6 models.

edges.description: Short stature is reported clinically, but the cellular-to-organism growth bridge has not been tested for TUBGCP6 patient variants.
intermediate_mechanisms: Developmental growth restriction downstream of impaired proliferation is hypothesized but untested for patient alleles.

edges.description: Reduced cerebral growth presents as congenital microcephaly.
Developmental delay is part of the reported cerebral phenotype.
Intellectual impairment accompanies the congenital brain phenotype.
Pachygyria is a directly imaged cortical malformation.

At this tissue-to-phenotype graph scale, reduced callosal area is an observed structural manifestation of abnormal cerebral development. This does not establish the upstream cellular mechanism or a disease-wide frequency.
A hypoplastic vermis is a directly imaged structural manifestation at the cerebral-development tissue endpoint.
Seizures occurred in a minority of the original cohort.
Underdeveloped retina and choroid produce the defining ocular morphology.
The ocular abnormality is accompanied by early visual impairment.
Vitreoretinal traction creates points at risk for retinal detachment.
Reduced somatic growth is clinically expressed as short stature.

nodes.description: Human findings include congenital severe microcephaly, diffuse pachygyria, small cerebral hemispheres, cerebellar vermis hypoplasia, developmental and intellectual impairment, and occasional seizures. Later reports extend the imaging spectrum to agyria/pachygyria, ventriculomegaly, and abnormal sulcation. These observations define the tissue endpoint rather than proving the upstream cellular bridge.

evidence.snippet: Here we identify mutations in the genes encoding PLK4 kinase, a master regulator of centriole duplication, and its substrate TUBGCP6 in individuals with microcephalic primordial dwarfism and additional congenital anomalies, including retinopathy, thereby extending the human phenotypic spectrum associated with centriole dysfunction.

nodes.description: The 2023 disease review describes biallelic TUBGCP6 variants as loss-of-function, and reported alleles include sequence changes and deletions. That disease-level assignment still requires allele-level calibration: the founding p.Ter1820Gly read-through allele was predicted to extend the protein or promote non-stop-mediated decay but was not functionally tested in the founding report. Acute depletion of TUBGCP6 in DLD-1 cells models reduced protein availability, not any specific patient genotype.
